noticias.titulo: US Defence Secretary Hegseth reveals military partnership on Venezuela trip
noticias.resumen: Pete Hegseth says the agreement will include joint training and intelligence sharing with the Venezuelan military.
noticias.texto:
US Defence Secretary Hegseth reveals military partnership on Venezuela trip
Pete Hegseth says the agreement will include joint training and intelligence sharing with the Venezuelan military.
United States Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth has announced a new agreement with Venezuela’s interim government to facilitate military cooperation between the two countries.
The Pentagon chief made a surprise visit to the Venezuelan capital of Caracas on Wednesday, becoming the latest in a series of high-level officials under US President Donald Trump to travel to the South American country.
During his stop, Hegseth revealed that the deal would include intelligence sharing and joint training for the two countries’ militaries.
“We see this as a reestablishment of our defence partnership and the opportunity to work together between our two great militaries,” he said.
Their shared aim would be “to stabilise Venezuela and rid it of narco-terrorists once and for all”, Hegseth added.
Hegseth was hosted by interim President Delcy Rodriguez, who has led the government since her swearing-in on January 5. His trip was not previously announced by the Pentagon.
The Trump administration has exerted heavy influence over Rodriguez and her government after abducting former President Nicolas Maduro during a military attack on January 3.
Rodriguez was previously Venezuela’s vice president. Trump has justified the attack as a law enforcement effort designed to force Maduro to “stand trial on American soil”, charging him with weapons- and drug-related crimes.
After the operation, Trump also said he planned to “run” Venezuela, and he told The Atlantic magazine that Rodriguez could “pay a very big price, probably bigger than Maduro” if she refuses to comply with US demands.
Since then, he has worked with the Venezuelan government to extract concessions on US priorities such as energy development and military cooperation.
Critics have accused the US of reducing Venezuela to a vassal state and exploiting its resources while leaving Maduro’s government largely intact.
Under Maduro, the Venezuelan state was accused of human rights abuses including torture, arbitrary imprisonment and extrajudicial killings.
Still, Trump has held up Venezuela as a model he would like to see replicated in other countries, like Iran and Cuba.
In Wednesday’s remarks, Hegseth said that the South American country “has gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner”.
Rodriguez hailed the agreement as a “resumption of the technical-military relationship between both countries”, and she expressed hope that their cooperation could be “brought to its highest possible level”.
Hegseth is also set to meet with officials in Colombia later on Wednesday as part of a trip to the region.
Colombian Defence Minister Jorge Eduardo Mora said on Tuesday that the US would deliver a C-130 Hercules military aircraft, as the US steps up military involvement across Latin America.
Hegseth has faced pressure to step down from his role, following a midterm election in which the US-Israel war on Iran contributed to Republican losses across the country.
A key member of Trump’s cabinet, Hegseth has championed the war, as well as efforts to weaken rules of engagement designed to limit civilian casualties.
Hegseth narrowly avoided a recent impeachment effort in the US Congress this month. The sponsor of that effort, outgoing Republican US Representative Thomas Massie, cited the Iran war as well as a campaign of military strikes targeting alleged drug trafficking vessels off the coast of Latin America.
The boat-strike campaign has killed an estimated 244 people and has been denounced as extrajudicial killings by legal experts.

noticias.titulo: What does Israel’s new ground offensive mean for Palestinians in Gaza?
noticias.resumen: Israeli tanks advance beyond the 'Yellow Line', forcing Palestinians to flee again in Gaza.
noticias.texto:
What does Israel’s new ground offensive mean for Palestinians in Gaza?
Israeli tanks advance beyond the ‘Yellow Line’, forcing Palestinians to flee again as Gaza faces a deepening humanitarian crisis.
Israeli forces have launched a ground operation in central Gaza, advancing west of the line they withdrew to under last year’s ceasefire and forcing Palestinian families, many of whom had already been displaced, to flee their homes once again.
The operation, the first major ground offensive publicly announced by the Israeli military since the ceasefire took effect on October 10, 2025, follows a warning by the United States-backed Board of Peace that the 13-month-old agreement risks collapse. In a report to the United Nations Security Council, the board accused Israel of restricting aid and delaying the deployment of Palestinian police, and Hamas of continuing armed activity and taxing goods entering Gaza. Senior Hamas official Basem Naim dismissed the report as “pure disinformation”.
What happened in central Gaza on Wednesday?
Israeli tanks and bulldozers advanced towards Salah al-Din Street, Gaza’s main north-south route, east of the Nuseirat refugee camp and north of the Bureij refugee camp, Al Jazeera correspondents reported. Palestinians fled those areas, amid heavy gunfire and artillery shelling.
The Israeli military body overseeing civilian affairs in the occupied Palestinian territory, known as COGAT, said the army had closed that stretch of Salah al-Din Street and told residents to stay away until further notice. The army hasn’t said how long the operation will last.
An Israeli attack on al-Mughraqa killed one person and wounded several others, an official at al-Awda Hospital told Al Jazeera. Separate attacks in Deir el-Balah, Nuseirat and Gaza City killed three more people.
“We fear this may be the start of a broader operation and that displacement will begin anew, as we have not yet recovered from the effects of the previous war and displacement,” Mahmoud al-Saafin, a 27-year-old resident of Bureij, told the AFP news agency.
The areas targeted in the operation lie west of the “Yellow Line”, where Israeli troops pulled back to under the first phase of President Donald Trump’s plan, leaving them in about 53 percent of Gaza. Israel has, however, continued to move that line gradually, and it now encompasses around two-thirds of the enclave. More than two million Palestinians live in the rest, mostly in tents.
Why does Israel say it launched the operation?
The military told AFP it had launched “a precise operation” west of the line “to remove a threat” posed to the Israeli army, adding that “there is Hamas infrastructure in the area, adding it was responding to Hamas ceasefire violations.
“We reserve the freedom to act and manoeuvre whenever necessary to eliminate any immediate threat in the Gaza Strip,” the army said.
Israel says Hamas has been regrouping and rearming, and it has stepped up attacks. On Saturday, an Israeli attack killed Samir Abu Younis, the Qassam Brigades’ Rafah commander.
Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said Israel won’t withdraw until Hamas is dismantled. “If tensions escalate on the various fronts, we are fully prepared to seize additional territory, evacuate local residents and incorporate it into Israel’s permanent security perimeter,” he said.
How have Palestinian groups, including Hamas, responded?
Hamas called the operation and the forced evacuations northeast of Nuseirat “a dangerous development and a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement”, and urged mediators to “intervene immediately”.
It accused Israel of “systematically” squeezing Palestinians into a narrow area of Gaza, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s caretaker government of escalating to escape its domestic crises.
Hamas also condemned the Board of Peace for having “unacceptably equated the occupation’s ongoing aggression with the suffering of the Palestinian victim”.
The Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine called the operation a “prelude” to a wider escalation aimed at forcibly displacing Palestinians.
Has Israel violated the Gaza ceasefire before?
Israeli forces have kept up near-daily attacks, shelling and home demolitions. Gaza’s Ministry of Health says they have killed 1,658 Palestinians and wounded 6,000 since the ceasefire began. The Israeli military says five of its soldiers have been killed in the same period, the Reuters news agency reports.
On Tuesday alone, Israeli fire killed six Palestinians, including a six-year-old boy, Gaza’s civil defence agency and hospitals told AFP.
Aid remains restricted. About 100,000 tents are waiting to enter Gaza, held up by crossing closures and lengthy Israeli security checks, the International Organization for Migration says.
Where does the ceasefire stand?
The ceasefire halted major fighting, but the rest of the plan, covering Israel’s withdrawal, reconstruction and Hamas’s disarmament, has stalled. Hamas agreed in July to a roadmap to give up its weapons and hand over governance. Israel rejected it.
Israel also hasn’t let the board’s technocratic administration start work in Gaza. That has held up an international stabilisation force, The Associated Press news agency reported.
The board spelled out what failure would mean. “Should it collapse, there would be no road map to return to, no administration to deploy and no enabling environment to rebuild.”

noticias.titulo: Pew Research: Islam on track to become world’s largest religion by 2035
noticias.resumen: The report projects steady increases for both Christianity and Islam from 2020 to 2070.
noticias.texto:
Pew Research: Islam on track to become world’s largest religion by 2035
The report projects steady increases for both Christianity and Islam from 2020 to 2070.
Islam will soon be the world’s largest religion, taking Christianity’s place by 2035, according to the Pew Research Center.
The research organisation assessed the Muslim population’s expected growth in a report released on Tuesday, which projected that both groups will see their numbers increase over the next few decades.
However, the Muslim population will “simply [grow] at a faster pace,” the report said.
The projection analysed 201 countries and territories, accounting for 99.98 percent of the population, and spanned the geographic distribution and future changes of seven religious groups and affiliations – Muslims, Christians, Jews, Hindus, Buddhists, and others – from the years 2020 to 2070.
The results are part of the Pew-Templeton Global Religious Futures Project, which seeks to analyse religious change and its impact on the world.
The organisation stressed that the findings are “not intended to predict all the ways the world could change” as several other events might occur that could impact a group’s religious affiliation, such as socioeconomic circumstances, natural disasters, and wars.
Baby boom
According to the report, Muslims give birth to the highest number of children, one of the factors that Pew says make them the world’s fastest-growing religious group.
Fertility rates were found to be 3.1 children per Muslim woman, while Christians, with the second-highest fertility rate, had 2.5 children per Christian woman.
A generation can typically replace itself with a fertility rate of around 2.1 children per woman.
Both groups are expected to “keep pace with the world’s overall population growth”, according to Pew.
Muslims could gain up to 1.6 billion people through natural population change, compared to 792 million people for Christians.
Estimated losses
Muslims are expected to have much smaller losses in their community than Christians leaving or converting religions.
“The difference between the number of people who join and leave Islam is expected to result in a loss of 8 million people during the projection period, [whereas] for Christians, the net difference is a projected loss of 105 million people,” the report said.
Those who choose to depart from Christianity may not identify with a religion afterwards, including atheists and agnostics.
However, the research finds that Islam’s projected growth is not the result of people converting from Christianity: the number of Muslims projected to convert to Christianity is only “slightly greater” than the number of Christians expected to become Muslims.
Country dynamics
Between 2020 and 2070, “most of the growth in the world’s Muslim population is projected to occur in places where Muslims already make up a majority of the population”, said Pew.
By 2070, Muslims will make up 95 percent of the population in the Middle East-North Africa region. Meanwhile, in the Asia-Pacific region, Muslims are expected to surpass the religiously unaffiliated.
Muslims were the majority religious group in 53 countries in 2020. An additional 1.2 billion Muslims are expected to live in these countries by 2070, representing 74 percent of the projected growth of the global Muslim population.
For instance, Pakistan’s Muslim population is expected to double from 227 million in 2020 to 461 million in 2070. The country will become the world’s largest Muslim population, overtaking Indonesia, Pew said.
Christian growth will also be concentrated across 120 countries where Christians were already the majority of the population.
Overall, the population of Christians in these countries is forecast to rise by 630 million, representing 92 percent of global Christian growth.

noticias.titulo: Florida pastor found guilty over 2021 assassination of Haitian president
noticias.resumen: Christian Emmanuel Sanon faces life in prison after conviction on charges arising from killing of Jovenel Moïse A Florida pastor with dual Haitian-American citizenship was convicted on Wednesday of US charges arising from the 2021 assassination of the Haitian president Jovenel Moïse. Christian Emmanuel Sanon was found guilty on charges including conspiring to kill Moïse after a nearly eight-week trial in federal court in Miami. He had faced a total of eight charges including conspiracy to kidnap or kill a person outside the United States. Continue reading...
noticias.texto:
A Florida pastor with dual Haitian-American citizenship was convicted on Wednesday of US charges arising from the 2021 assassination of the Haitian president Jovenel Moïse.
Christian Emmanuel Sanon was found guilty on charges including conspiring to kill Moïse after a nearly eight-week trial in federal court in Miami. He had faced a total of eight charges including conspiracy to kidnap or kill a person outside the United States.
He faces up to life in prison at sentencing.
Federal prosecutors said south Florida was a hub for planning and financing the plot to oust Moïse and install a president of the conspirators’ choosing. The government said Sanon was the conspirators’ initial choice for Moïse’s replacement. Prosecutors also said Sanon helped raise money for the conspiracy and arranged travel to Haiti and lodging for himself and others in that country.
Sanon acknowledged in trial testimony that he was in communication at one point with people trying to replace Moïse, but pointed out that the group had moved on to another candidate long before the assassination. He denied any knowledge of plans to kill Moïse.
Sanon was born in Haiti and moved to the US as a teenager. He testified that he worked with churches in Haitian immigrant communities in Florida and the midwest.
Haiti has not had a president since authorities said that a squad of mostly retired Colombian soldiers killed Moïse and wounded his wife in a night-time raid at their home on 7 July 2021. The poorest country in the Americas, Haiti has a history of dictatorship, political upheaval and foreign intervention that has long hindered democratic rule.
The election of a new president is scheduled for next year.
Prosecutors said the scheme to kill Moïse included paying about two dozen foreign mercenaries with money obtained from US government programs that were intended to help businesses during the Covid pandemic, according to court records. US prosecutors have charged more than 40 people with crimes related to the assassination and a dozen have been convicted, including five who are serving life sentences.
The plot to oust Moïse began taking final shape in April 2021, when Sanon met in south Florida with a former Haitian senator and several US businesspeople, according to an indictment. The group agreed that Sanon, once in power, would award contracts to two Florida-based companies – Counter Terrorist Unit Federal Academy and Counter Terrorist Unit Security, collectively known as CTU – for infrastructure projects, security forces and military equipment, according to investigators.
CTU initially hired about 18 Colombian nationals with military training to provide security for Sanon, according to prosecutors. Conspirators also spent months obtaining weapons and body armor and attempting to build ties with Haitian gangs, officials said.
By June 2021, the conspirators realized Sanon had neither the constitutional qualifications nor sufficient popular support to become president. They shifted their support to Wendelle Coq Thélot, a former Haitian supreme court judge who died in January 2025 while a fugitive.
Sanon was previously scheduled to be tried with four other men who were convicted earlier this year, but his case was separated from theirs and delayed for health reasons.

noticias.titulo: Jensen Huang to testify before Congress on ‘potential breach of national security’
noticias.resumen: High-stakes hearing comes in wake of resignation from Nvidia after alleged affair with suspected Chinese spy Nvidia’s former CEO Jensen Huang will testify before several congressional committees on 1 December, setting the stage for a high-stakes hearing in the wake of his resignation following an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Tim Teter, Nvidia’s general counsel, has also agreed to appear for a closed-door transcribed interview the following day, 2 December. Continue reading...
noticias.texto:
Nvidia’s former CEO Jensen Huang will testify before several congressional committees on 1 December, setting the stage for a high-stakes hearing in the wake of his resignation following an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
Tim Teter, Nvidia’s general counsel, has also agreed to appear for a closed-door transcribed interview the following day, 2 December.
“We look forward to hearing from Jensen Huang and Tim Teter on their roles in a potential breach of our national security,” Congressmen Brian Mast, John Moolenaar and Rick Crawford, who chair the committees, said in a press release. “The American people need answers on Mr Huang and Nvidia’s role in allowing dangerous [People’s Republic of China] actors to access our most advanced chips, as well as the role of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in this scandal.”
The three congressmen chair the foreign affairs committee, the select committee on the Chinese Communist party, and the intelligence committee of the House of Representatives, respectively. On 12 November, they had signed a letter warning Huang that he could face a subpoena if he did not agree to the closed-door meeting.
Nvidia chips are key to powering the artificial intelligence boom. The Trump administration has prohibited the selling of advanced artificial intelligence chips to China.
Huang stepped down as Nvidia’s CEO after allegations of extramarital relationships with the suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang and two Nvidia employees surfaced.
Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, had been Megaspeed International’s executive director. The Singapore-based cloud computing company has bought nearly $5bn in AI chips and advanced hardware. The company said Alice Huang stepped down in 2025.
Megaspeed ultimately facilitated about $12bn in chip sales, in violation of US export controls. On Friday, Malaysia stated that they were investigating whether the company diverted advanced AI ships to other countries.
A recent joint Department of Commerce and Department of Justice letter, stated that the Department of Commerce, under its secretary, Howard Lutnick, first started an investigation in Megaspeed on 2024 for potential export control violations. The justice department, led by the attorney general, Todd Blanche, took over in 2025.
In his first remarks since his resignation, Jensen Huang said on Thursday he would be willing to return to Nvidia as CEO. Elon Musk and other Silicon Valley tech giants, along with 165,000 signatories to an open letter, have called for his reinstatement. Trump has also signaled his openness for the disgraced tech CEO’s return.

noticias.titulo: Hi-tech Shenzhen takes centre stage as Xi sends ‘Chinamaxxing’ message at Apec summit
noticias.resumen: Host city offers showcase of China’s rise into a confident and innovative power central to global economy In a Shenzhen square on a balmy evening, locals and tourists watched the dozens of glinting towers that make up the city’s skyline ripple through the colour spectrum – cyan and violet, cyber green, China’s national scarlet and gold – repeatedly flashing the words “Apec 2026”. The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is a dream showcase for one of China’s most advanced cities, and the country’s leader, Xi Jinping, is basking in its neon glow. Continue reading...
noticias.texto:
In a Shenzhen square on a balmy evening, locals and tourists watched the dozens of glinting towers that make up the city’s skyline ripple through the colour spectrum – cyan and violet, cyber green, China’s national scarlet and gold – repeatedly flashing the words “Apec 2026”.
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is a dream showcase for one of China’s most advanced cities, and the country’s leader, Xi Jinping, is basking in its neon glow.
On the sidelines, a series of high-profile bilateral meetings and the announcement of a historic three-way summit with Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin have cemented Xi’s status as an agenda setter on the global stage.
The broader Apec summit, meanwhile, provides an opportunity for China to present itself as a steward of multilateralism against what it terms “unilateralism and protectionism” – that is to say, trade measures taken against Beijing by countries such as the US.
All this is set against the futuristic backdrop that is Shenzhen, a city that perhaps better than no other embodies China’s rise into a confident, technologically innovative power central to the global economy.
A photo display in the Apec media centre charts Shenzhen’s transformation from sparsely populated marshland, calling it “a miracle in the history of world development created by the Chinese people”.
“[Xi] wants people to go home Chinamaxxing,” said Prof Astrid Nordin, of King’s College London. “Shenzhen is itself part of the message. It’s a showcase of Chinese technological and economic achievements, and of China’s claim that it offers opportunities for prosperity in a world increasingly characterised by uncertainty and conflict.”
Like the light show, the summit is being carefully coordinated. The Financial Times cited people familiar with the matter as saying it would be one of the most tightly controlled in the organisation’s history, with leaders having to travel to a state guesthouse beside Shenzhen’s tiger safari park to meet Xi. The paper said diplomats had grumbled that the format “seems designed to reduce the free-flowing discussion characteristic of prior editions”.
Setting out its expectations for the summit, China’s foreign ministry has said it looks forward to “practical results in key areas such as trade, connectivity, digital economy, AI and so on”.
Already, Xi has announced trade wins with Canada’s Mark Carney, extending remission measures for certain Chinese steel and aluminium products by two years in exchange for tariff relief on Canadian pork, fish and seafood exports.
A meeting with Papua New Guinea’s leader, meanwhile, showed how Beijing’s geopolitical priorities have been absorbed and reflected by its allies, with James Marape recounting to Xi how he had closed Taiwan’s office in his country despite domestic challenges in doing so.
The most important meeting will be between Xi and Trump. The leaders of the world’s two superpowers are expected to tackle a broad range of issues including AI and trade. In a move that could strain the fragile tariff truce that the two leaders first agreed last year, the Trump administration said on Monday it would further restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips.
Christopher Adams, a senior adviser at the law firm Covington who was at the centre of trade negotiations with China for the Obama and first Trump administrations, said: “The trade truce may increasingly look like a ceasefire in a war where major combat operations remain on hold but skirmishes are escalating to the point where the line between peace and war is blurred.
“I don’t see pressure to announce a further extension of the trade truce in Shenzhen. If a significant extension is announced, that would be an upside surprise.”
China has not hesitated to leverage Apec’s multinational platform in service of its arguments. A commentary by the state news agency Xinhua on Tuesday said: “Amid deepening geopolitical rivalries and growing global divisions, [China’s hosting] sends a clear signal that great-power competition need not be a zero-sum game, and that one country’s development need not come at the expense of another.”
The chair of the Apec senior officials’ meeting, Chen Xu, said Beijing had made trade “openness” a key focus of its Apec year and looked forward to “achieving more practical outcomes on the trade front”.
The much anticipated trilateral summit with Trump and Putin, on the other hand, could prove largely symbolic. For Xi, “it provides the appearance of China shaping the world order as an equal to the United States,” said Dr Kevork Oskanian, an expert on Russia at the University of Exeter. “Agreement on substantial issues, which would, in any case, require extensive preparatory negotiations, is unlikely.”
For China’s ruling Communist party, the political pomp has another key purpose. Nordin said summits were “occasions for leaders to tell stories about the world, about their country’s place in it … and one of the most important audiences for those stories is at home.”
For the locals watching the skyscraper light show on Monday night, the symbolism was not lost. China’s export might had helped it become increasingly powerful on the world stage, said one local man, who did not give his name. “It’s so great that the summit will take place in Shenzhen,” he said. “I feel very proud.”

noticias.titulo: Hundreds arrested in anti-Trump protests in Philippines amid anger over Iran war and AI pact
noticias.resumen: Organisers say up to 10,000 people could join next round of demonstrations as US president arrives for Asean summit Asean and Apec summits – as it happened Hundreds of people have been arrested in heated demonstrations against Donald Trump in Manila, as the US president arrived in the city for a leaders’ summit. Organisers claimed as many as 10,000 people would be joining protests against Trump in the capital of the Philippines on Tuesday, where he is attending the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit. The crowds were expected to try to march to the summit site. Continue readi
noticias.texto:
Hundreds of people have been arrested in heated demonstrations against Donald Trump in Manila, as the US president arrived in the city for a leaders’ summit.
Organisers claimed as many as 10,000 people would be joining protests against Trump in the capital of the Philippines on Tuesday, where he is attending the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit. The crowds were expected to try to march to the summit site.
Authorities have arrested nearly 300 people in widespread protests held in the days leading up to the summit, with large parts of the capital closed off and tight security in place.
Some burned effigies of Trump and faced off with police officers armed with batons and shields. Slogans on placards called the American leader the world’s “No 1 terrorist” in protests held on Monday.
Demonstrators angry at the cost of living and energy shock caused by the Iran war, and the new US-led Pax Silica initiative on AI and critical minerals, tried to reach the summit at the Philippine International Convention Center on Monday, but were blocked by police.
Pax Silica has sparked tensions in the Philippines over plans to build a tech hub outside Manila that critics say will affect water and energy supplies, and displace members of the Ayta Indigenous community.
Large sections of central Manila were closed to the public as part of the security cordon and public holidays put in place for the Asean summit.
After departing from Fairbanks in Alaska, Trump emerged from Air Force One at Ninoy Aquino International airport at 5.54pm local time (0954 GMT), live video showed.
Trump will meet with the leaders of Australia, Japan and India on Tuesday night before heading to Shenzhen in China on Wednesday. There he will attend the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit and hold trilateral talks with China’s president, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin of Russia.
The backlash against Trump follows the ousting of the boss of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, and allegations members of the US administration, including the commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, knew about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
Trump’s delegation was expected to include Elon Musk.
Protest leader Renato Reyes blamed the arrests in Manila on the heavy handed response of the government on the president, Ferdinand Marcos Jr, calling Monday the largest single day of police arrests since Marcos came to office in 2022.
“It is really crazy that the Philippine government is rolling out the red carpet for someone who has been so flatly rejected by the American people,” Reyes said. “Trump started a war that devastated the global economy and pushed oil prices in the Philippines to historic highs. It has caused untold suffering on the Filipino people.
“So, yes, Trump will have to pay for his crimes and he will have to be answerable, not just to the American people, but to the people of the world.”
The Philippine national police said some officers were injured during confrontations with demonstrators opposed to the summit, including when objects were allegedly thrown at officers.
Pax Silica will include a technology hub planned at New Clark City in Tarlac, about 100km from Manila.
Intended to bolster western stocks of AI technology and reduce “excessive dependencies” on single source supply chains, including from China, Pax Silica will provide chips and critical minerals to 26 participating signatory governments.
Amnesty International said demonstrations should not be forcibly or violently dispersed.
“Reports of arrests during the protests demand immediate scrutiny,” Amnesty’s director for the Philippines, Ritz Lee Santos III, said. “Authorities must explain the specific grounds for each arrest and any continued detention. Anyone detained solely for peacefully exercising their rights must be released immediately.”

noticias.titulo: General Pants Co enters voluntary administration, putting hundreds of jobs at risk
noticias.resumen: Australian fashion chain becomes latest retailer in trouble after David Jones, Cue and Veronika Maine Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Youth fashion chain General Pants Co has become the latest major retailer to slide into voluntary administration, putting nearly 500 jobs at risk as Australia’s retail sector continues to struggle with cash-strapped shoppers and online-only competitors. The collapse comes not long after that of upmarket department store David Jones and premium womenswear brands Cue and Veronika Maine, underscoring the mounting toll of tough economic
noticias.texto:
Youth fashion chain General Pants Co has become the latest major retailer to slide into voluntary administration, putting nearly 500 jobs at risk as Australia’s retail sector continues to struggle with cash-strapped shoppers and online-only competitors.
The collapse comes not long after that of upmarket department store David Jones and premium womenswear brands Cue and Veronika Maine, underscoring the mounting toll of tough economic conditions on established retailers.
The consultancy Alvarez & Marsal confirmed it had taken control of General Pants Co and nine related businesses after being appointed their voluntary administrator late on Wednesday evening.
In a statement, the administrators said they were working closely with the existing management team to undertake an urgent assessment of the business, including its trading performance, stores, stock and costs.
All 35 General Pants Co stores and its online store would remain open and trading as usual while the administrators worked out whether they could sell or restructure the business to keep it afloat, the firm said.
Guardian Australia contacted General Pants Co’s parent company, Alquemie group, for comment on Thursday morning.
Alvarez & Marsal said the 500 people employed by General Pants Co across Australia and New Zealand would continue to be paid for the work they did during the administration period.
Additionally, the consultancy said staff entitlements accrued prior to the appointment remained legally protected under the Corporations Act and of a higher priority to administrators than “most” other unsecured creditor claims.
Two of the Alvarez & Marsal managing directors, Jason Tracy and Glen Kanevsky, were appointed to oversee the administration, with a first meeting with creditors due to be held on 30 November.
Tracy described General Pants Co as “one of Australia’s best-known youth fashion brands, with a loyal customer base and a dedicated team”.
He said the administrators’ immediate priorities were to keep the stores trading, support employees and customers, and pursue “a sale and/or recapitalisation” of the business.
“With Black Friday next week, we are focused on maximising trading performance and expect strong demand over the period,” Tracy said.
“We thank the team members, landlords and suppliers of General Pants Co for their support as we work through the administration.”
General Pants Co, which began in 1972 as a specialty denim store on Sydney’s George Street and has traded across Australia and New Zealand since, is not the only Australian retailer under significant pressure.
Last week, the embattled upmarket retailer David Jones entered administration with more than $400m owed to creditors. Less than two months earlier, Cue Clothing Co, the owner of mainstay Australian labels Cue and Veronika Maine, entered administration and receivership in September.
Last year, Mosaic Group, the owner of brands including Noni B, Rivers, and Katies, was liquidated.
While Australian retailers deal with their own increased operating costs, indebted households are tightened their budgets during a new bout of inflationary pressures.
This strain is driving a sharp contraction across the sector, according to credit reporting agency Equifax, marked by surging business closures and a slowdown in new brands.
Equifax’s Brad Walters said that the strain was not limited to large retailers such as David Jones.
“Smaller retailers are also dealing with a difficult combination of softer discretionary spending, rising operating costs and increasingly narrow financial buffers,” Walters said.
“Instead of funding long-term expansion, smaller operators are taking on credit simply to manage immediate overheads.”
While David Jones is closing half of its 38-store network, rival Myer is facing its own financial stress, with the chain forced to offer “higher than planned promotional activity to stimulate demand”.
Four out of Myer’s five newly acquired apparel chains – Jay Jays, Portmans, Dotti, and Jacqui E – recorded falling sales last financial year, leaving Just Jeans as the sole brand to post growth.

noticias.titulo: Australia may have ‘one foot in recession’ as unemployment surges to five-year high
noticias.resumen: Jobless rate rises from 4.7% to 4.9% for October, latest bureau of statistics figures reveal Get our daily political email , free app or daily news podcast Australia may already have “one foot in recession” after unemployment surged to 4.9% in October, from 4.7%, in a shock increase that will add to rising worries this year’s five interest rate hikes have pushed the economy past a tipping point. New figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics showed the number of employed people dropped by 43,500 in the month, confounding forecasts for jobs growth and a steady jobless rate. Continue readi
noticias.texto:
Australia may already have “one foot in recession” after unemployment surged to 4.9% in October, from 4.7%, in a shock increase that will add to rising worries this year’s five interest rate hikes have pushed the economy past a tipping point.
New figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics showed the number of employed people dropped by 43,500 in the month, confounding forecasts for jobs growth and a steady jobless rate.
After starting the year at 4%, unemployment has now lifted to its highest level in five years to approach pre-Covid levels. In a further sign of deteriorating conditions, the number of employed Australians has dropped in three of the past four months.
David Bassanese, the chief economist at Betashares, said there were lingering questions over the seasonal movements in the labour force data that could be giving a falsely weak picture of the jobs market.
“If these employment declines prove to be real, however, they’re the type of weakness that could well mean we’ve seen the last interest rate hike,” Bassanese said.
“Indeed, consecutive large employment declines might suggest the economy already has one foot in recession.”
The shock figures validate warnings from the three dissenting Reserve Bank of Australia board members, who voted against the Melbourne Cup day rate hike and warned of a “materially sharper downturn” in the economy as households struggled to deal with this year’s substantial lift in borrowing costs.
Full-time employment dropped by 2,900 in October, the ABS data showed, and part-time employment by a steeper 40,600 people.
Sunny Nguyen, the head of Australia economics at Moody’s Analytics, said “the Aussie labour market has unmistakenly turned”.
Nguyen said the latest data “all but closes the door” on any chance of a pre-Christmas rate hike.
“For the RBA, this lands on a board already split over whether policy has gone far enough,” he said.
“The bank only lifted its unemployment forecast earlier this month to peak above 5% by the end of 2028; the labour market is within sight of that level two years early.”

noticias.titulo: Beau Lamarre-Condon’s testimony about Jesse Baird and Luke Davies’ deaths ‘fanciful in the extreme’, crown alleges
noticias.resumen: Prosecutor argues accused could be convicted on strength of forensic and ballistics evidence alone in closing statement Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Beau Lamarre-Condon’s claims about the deaths of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies are “fanciful in the extreme”, a court has heard. The former police officer is accused of fatally shooting Baird and his new partner, Davies, with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney on 19 February 2024. Continue reading...
noticias.texto:
Beau Lamarre-Condon’s claims about the deaths of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies are “fanciful in the extreme”, a court has heard.
The former police officer is accused of fatally shooting Baird and his new partner, Davies, with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney on 19 February 2024.
He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter.
The crown prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC began delivering his closing statement on Thursday as the double murder trial entered its ninth week.
The defence had argued the two men died in struggles with the accused when he acted in “self-defence”.
Lamarre-Condon had previously told the court he was aiming to shoot Baird in the shoulder to get him to drop a knife, and accidentally shot him a second time as they fell to the ground.
But Hatfield told the court the injury from the first shot would cause someone to pass out.
“Common sense renders it completely improbable that you could suffer such an injury yet immediately grab hold of a pistol with your left and forcefully pull a person brandishing it to the ground,” Hatfield said.
“Such a scenario, you might think, is fanciful in the extreme.”
He argued Lamarre-Condon could be convicted on the strength of the forensic and ballistics evidence alone.
Forensic evidence of the directionality of the bullet and the wounds on Baird’s body indicated Lamarre-Condon shot Baird in the back as the other man fled towards the back door, Hatfield alleged.
The height of the bullet marks meant Baird must have been ducking or stooping at the time, according to the prosecution.
Hatfield said the near-vertical trajectory of the bullet through the floor spoke to a controlled shot through Baird’s temple, with the prosecutor calling it an “execution-style shot”.
The timing between the two shots allowed only for a quick two to three steps, the crown prosecutor told the court.
“Not the bizarre wrestling and yanking the accused has described,” Hatfield said.
At this point, Davies must have realised something was “seriously amiss”, the prosecutor said, and attempted to call triple zero.
There was no doubt he was then killed by a bullet that passed through the door and into his head, Hatfield said, telling the court there was gunshot stippling on the door but not the body.
Aspects of the defence’s case, that Baird lunged at Lamarre-Condon with a knife and that Davies picked up the gun and pointed it at the accused, came only from the former officer himself, Hatfield said.
“Nothing independent of him supports any of what he said about those events,” Hatfield told the jury.
The trial before Justice Natalie Adams continues.

noticias.titulo: GTA 6 dazzles gamers in Australia with ‘fully lived-in, breathable world’
noticias.resumen: Players can renovate houses, fix cars, lift weights and follow the story in Grand Theft Auto VI’s Miami-inspired Vice City Tell us: are you playing Grand Theft Auto VI? Gamers across Australia woke up Thursday morning feeling like Christmas had come early, some bleary-eyed from late-night sessions on the PlayStation, others with grand plans for a weekend foray in Vice City when their day jobs let them loose. Grand Theft Auto VI, more than a decade in the making, is here. And the reviews, mere hours into release, reflect universal acclaim. The game has already vaulted to the top spot on Metacri
noticias.texto:
Gamers across Australia woke up Thursday morning feeling like Christmas had come early, some bleary-eyed from late-night sessions on the PlayStation, others with grand plans for a weekend foray in Vice City when their day jobs let them loose.
Grand Theft Auto VI, more than a decade in the making, is here. And the reviews, mere hours into release, reflect universal acclaim. The game has already vaulted to the top spot on Metacritic’s list of the best games of all time, sitting above 1998’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time with an unprecedented 99/100 score.
Australians who put in a few hours as soon as the game launched at 12am said they were already beyond impressed.
“I had it loaded up bang on midnight,” Pat, 26, told Guardian Australia. “I just got on straight away, it was like being a kid on Christmas morning.”
He spent about two hours exploring the world of Leonida and its metropolis – based heavily on Miami – and his initial thoughts echoed others who described the GTA VI release as the “moon landing” of gaming.
“This is a fully lived-in, breathable world. It’s so much more tangible than so many video games,” Pat said. “I was at a loss for words trying to express to my girlfriend how significant this is.”
Ziggy Grant, a longtime fan of the GTA series, spent Wednesday night farewelling the old games before ushering in the new. Grant bought a Japanese-style mini truck in the online version of GTA V, painted it chrome and drove it in a loop around the map with other fans of the franchise.
“I just thought I should do it, it was just a silly thing,” Grant, who lives in South Australia, said, joining many other players on an online server. Around 11.29pm, just before the release of VI in Australia, everyone started to ping away. “The last ride, I had to do it to pay homage to GTA online. … I just got in my biggest plane, and flew off.”
GTA VI was waiting for him. Grant played until about 4.30am before he ran out of steam, leaving the house early Thursday morning to restock up on supplies and “life support”.
The new game is already impressive in its realism.
“It’s a lot like the Gold Coast,” Grant said of GTA VI, adding he’s never missed the launch of a Rockstar product. “This is just like being in a subtropical place on a hot summer’s day. … Everything’s more deliberate, it’s not just this goofy game where you go in and do a rampage.”
“It’s like the world is so alive, it’s just assaulting your senses the whole time.”
Angus, 27, has the game downloaded and ready to play but had to be at work on Thursday, “which is unfortunate”. He and two friends have developed a detailed plan involving pizzas, beer and hour-long shifts on a shared TV on Thursday night into the early hours of Friday morning.
“The last one came out when I was pretty much in grade 8,” he said. “I just turned 27, and the hype hasn’t really gone at all. It’s the only game where I’ve genuinely felt excited, it’s like Christmas morning to be honest.
“I’m just really keen to get home and play it. Hopefully the work day goes quick.”
He took Friday off to get in as much time as he could, with the trio planning to pass the controller around between power naps.
Rockstar Games has yet to release data on how many copies of the game have sold, worldwide or in Australia. But internet data and banking trends show it is exceedingly popular.
NBN Co said internet traffic set an all-time record last Thursday when pre-orders for GTA VI went live. But that record was broken again on Wednesday night. The government enterprise behind the Australian broadband network said it saw the most data “ever moved in a single second”.
“Looks like a few Aussies left their GTA VI download to the last minute 👀,” NBN Co wrote on social media. “That’s enough data to download GTA VI at 212GB around 21 times. Every. Single. Second.”
Maggie Brennan, an online creator who streams under the banner retromaggie on Twitch, said the game had been fantastic so far.
“The graphics are beautiful, from the texture of the pores in the character’s skin to the air blowing through their hair. Rockstar have done an amazing job,” she said. “But that water! That water is beautiful.”
She said just hours in there was already an untold level of detail for players to interact with. Gamers can renovate their houses, fix their cars, lift weights and follow the story, all buttressed by Rockstar Games’ “unhinged madness that we all love”.
Up in Sydney, Pat said he plans to fit in GTA VI around his work schedule as much as possible, with the whole weekend already written off for time in Vice City.
“I was supposed to have a work event on tonight and it got cancelled,” he said, temporarily hopeful. “But it’s back on now. The amount of sorrow I felt … ”
“I might have to work from home tomorrow,” he added. “I think the light rail might not be running properly … ”

noticias.titulo: Mike Lynch’s superyacht had unidentified vulnerability to high winds, report finds
noticias.resumen: Bayesian, which sank off Sicily killing seven including tech tycoon, had not been fully assessed, say investigators The superyacht Bayesian, which sank in a storm off Sicily killing seven people including the tech tycoon Mike Lynch and his teenage daughter, was vulnerable to knockdown but crew were not aware as it had never been assessed at anchor with its sails down, the final report from the UK’s Marine Accident Investigations Branch (MAIB) has said. The 56-metre (184ft) vessel was anchored near the fishing port of Porticello when it sank during a violent storm shortly before dawn on 19 Augu
noticias.texto:
The superyacht Bayesian, which sank in a storm off Sicily killing seven people including the tech tycoon Mike Lynch and his teenage daughter, was vulnerable to knockdown but crew were not aware as it had never been assessed at anchor with its sails down, the final report from the UK’s Marine Accident Investigations Branch (MAIB) has said.
The 56-metre (184ft) vessel was anchored near the fishing port of Porticello when it sank during a violent storm shortly before dawn on 19 August 2024.
Lynch, 59, had been enjoying a voyage around Sicily with family and friends after his acquittal in a long-running fraud case regarding the sale of the technology company he founded, Autonomy, to Hewlett-Packard in 2011.
He and his 18-year-old daughter, Hannah, died, as did lawyer Chris Morvillo and his wife, Neda, banker Jonathan Bloomer and his wife, Judy, and the yacht’s chef, Recaldo Thomas. Nine other crew members and six guests were rescued.
The MAIB final report, published on Thursday, appears to contrast with recent reports from Italy, where prosecutors have reportedly blamed errors by the crew.
The MAIB report details how the yacht was hit “by extreme winds that were not explicitly forecast” of about 70 knots (80 mph), which knocked it on to its side in less than 15 seconds. It sank 18 minutes later.
Investigators found that the yacht’s vulnerability to strong winds had never been assessed for the conditions in which it was anchored, with its sails down and its retractable centreboard raised. The centreboard is a large underwater structure that helps a sailing vessel remain stable.
The extreme weather was most likely caused by a downburst – a powerful blast of air from a thunderstorm that hits the sea and spreads out with enormous force, the report said.
None of the life rafts on board automatically inflated or released from the vessel. The crew managed to release one manually. Survivors were rescued by crew from a nearby yacht, the Sir Robert Baden-Powell.
Rob Loder, the chief inspector of MAIB, said: “This accident developed with extraordinary speed. In just 14 minutes, calm conditions had given way to winds of at least 68 knots, which in less than 15 seconds pushed the yacht on to its side.
“Our investigation found that Bayesian had a vulnerability to high winds that was not recognised, because the yacht had never been assessed at anchor with its sails down. The extreme winds that night were also not explicitly forecast, so the crew had no warning of the risk.”
The report conveys the desperate minutes as the Bayesian was knocked down. Crew were alerted by sudden and severe winds of up to 30 knots at 03.55, and within two minutes the yacht listed starboard and the vessel began to drag anchor before the wind suddenly increased to about 70 knots.
“At 04.06 Bayesian violently heeled over 90 degrees to starboard, taking less than 15 seconds to do so. People, furniture and loose items fell across the deck. The generators shut down immediately and battery-supplied emergency lighting automatically turned on,” the report said.
Some guests, awoken by the listing and who had left their cabins, escaped. One couple used furniture drawers as an improvised ladder. Guests who managed to get to the flying bridge were instructed to swim away from the vessel and warned to stay clear of the mast and boom as it sank.
Passengers and crew who made it out gathered in the water, using a torch on a mobile to search for others. A crew member managed to swim back to the yacht to manually release one life raft from stowage. By 04.24 the life raft was inflated.
The investigation found that, with no sails set, Bayesian was vulnerable to knockdown in severe winds. This vulnerability was affected by its loading condition, apparent wind angle and the position of the centreboard, but had not been identified in the originally approved stability information available to the crew.
It said information contained in guidance provided to mariners did not provide sufficient detail of the impact of possible weather conditions to support decision-making. The weather forecast also did not indicate the risk of downbursts from the thunderstorms it predicted, it said.
Inquest proceedings in the UK are looking at the deaths of Mike and Hannah Lynch and Jonathan and Judy Bloomer, who were all British nationals.
The Maritime and Coastguard Agency is also investigating the sinking.

noticias.titulo: Crimea bridge has been attacked again, says Russian-installed governor
noticias.resumen: Assessment of damage is underway, days after two attacks that destroyed road section of key bridge across Kerch strait linking annexed peninsula to Russia A key bridge connecting annexed Crimea to Russia has been attacked again, a Russian-appointed regional governor has said, two days after Ukrainian strikes caused serious damage to it. “Following a new attack on the Crimean Bridge, traffic has been temporarily halted. All relevant services are on site and at work. An assessment of the damage is under way,” Sergei Aksyonov, the Kremlin-appointed governor of Crimea, wrote on Telegram. Continue
noticias.texto:
A key bridge connecting annexed Crimea to Russia has been attacked again, a Russian-appointed regional governor has said, two days after Ukrainian strikes caused serious damage to it.
“Following a new attack on the Crimean Bridge, traffic has been temporarily halted. All relevant services are on site and at work. An assessment of the damage is under way,” Sergei Aksyonov, the Kremlin-appointed governor of Crimea, wrote on Telegram.
Wednesday’s attack is third this week on the highly symbolic bridge that links Russia with Crimea, which it seized from Ukraine in 2014. A 227-metre section of the road spanning the Kerch strait was destroyed this week, but the rail corridor appears to be operable despite sustaining some damage.
The strike comes just hours before an unprecedented meeting between Russian president Vladimir Putin and his Chinese and American counterparts, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump, in China. One source in Ukraine’s armed forces said this week’s attacks were designed to embarrass Putin on the world stage. “The bridge is a symbol of Putin’s rule. Destroying it sends a message to the other two great leaders that Putin is not as strong as he pretends,” the person said.
For Ukraine, the bridge is a hated symbol of Russian arrogance and colonial thinking. Ukraine has previously declared that the bridge across the Kerch strait, built eight years ago, is illegal. Kyiv had tried twice to blow it up – with a truck bomb in 2022, and a sea drone the following year.
Earlier, Ukraine critically damaged the road section of the bridge in what President Volodymyr Zelenskyy hailed as an “unprecedented” military operation. A span of the bridge’s road section collapsed, but the railway line was still standing.
Zelesnkyy described the earlier attack as the culmination of a long and complex campaign to demolish the bridge, involving domestically produced drones and ballistic missiles. Palianytsia drones hit the road section of the bridge, while Neptune and other missiles targeted the adjacent rail section, he added.

noticias.titulo: EU proposes €45bn loan for Ukraine to avert cash crisis and boost defences
noticias.resumen: Von der Leyen says she wants to give Kyiv ‘strong hand’ in talks and is confident all 27 member states will back idea The EU executive has proposed a €45bn (£37.5bn) loan for Ukraine to help with a looming cash crisis and reinforce its defences, as Russia’s relentless bombardment continues. Announcing the plan to lend Kyiv the money in 2027, the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, said: “We think this is the best way to give Ukraine a strong hand at the negotiating table. And Ukraine only needs to repay once Russia pays for the damage it has caused in Ukraine.” Continue readin
noticias.texto:
The EU executive has proposed a €45bn (£37.5bn) loan for Ukraine to help with a looming cash crisis and reinforce its defences, as Russia’s relentless bombardment continues.
Announcing the plan to lend Kyiv the money in 2027, the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, said: “We think this is the best way to give Ukraine a strong hand at the negotiating table. And Ukraine only needs to repay once Russia pays for the damage it has caused in Ukraine.”
She expressed confidence all 27 member states would stand behind the loan, despite four central and eastern European countries having already ruled themselves out.
The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said he hoped for the swift adoption of the loan and was counting on the support of all EU member states: “Strong support for Ukraine is the best signal to Russia that this war must end,” he wrote on X.
Zelenskyy convinced EU leaders last month that his country faced a €70bn funding gap in 2027. The EU pledged to cover €45bn and wants Ukraine’s other allies to cover the rest.
Only 11 months ago, the EU agreed a €90bn loan for Ukraine, which was intended to cover two-thirds of Kyiv’s military and civilian needs in 2026 and 2027. But as Russia’s attacks have escalated, the cost of Ukraine’s defence and the toll of economic disruption continue to rise.
Andrius Kubilius, the EU defence commissioner, said Ukraine’s military spending was increasingly dominated by drones. Ukraine, he told reporters, expected Russia to use 10m drones this year and 20m in 2027. “Ukraine with EU assistance needs to match – and will match,” he said.
The EU loan is split into two parts: €25bn for weapons and €20bn for civilian needs, including funding essential services, such as schools and hospitals.
Von der Leyen expressed confidence that all member states would support the loan because “all 27 member states say very clearly that they want to support Ukraine”. She said member states could choose to support Ukraine’s civilian needs, rather than military spending.
Slovakia, Czechia, Hungary and Bulgaria, however, have said they do not intend to take part in the latest funding round for Ukraine, prompting a warning from the German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, that he would block the EU’s seven-year budget unless all countries got onboard.
The four central and eastern countries are net beneficiaries of the EU budget, while Germany is the largest payer and Ukraine’s biggest EU donor.
The EU wants Ukraine’s non-EU allies – such as Norway, the UK and Canada – to find €25bn for Kyiv in 2027.
The EU proposal included provisions “to help other countries to help us”, a senior commission official said. Brussels has proposed that G7 countries that provide new loans get guarantees that the borrowing can be repaid with future profits from Russia’s frozen assets.
The profits from the Russian assets are being used to repay a €45bn loan issued by the G7 to Ukraine in 2024.
Countries with a triple-A credit rating could opt to provide guarantees to the EU budget up to €5bn to expand European borrowing for Ukraine on capital markets. The commission has identified six countries that fall into this category: Australia, Canada, Liechtenstein, Norway, Singapore and Switzerland.
EU officials previously said the UK and other allies needed to do more to support Ukraine in 2027, arguing that the EU was shouldering too much of the burden. The UK subsequently pledged a £10bn economic and military support package for Ukraine.
Zelenskyy said: “The UK, Canada, Japan, and Norway have been helping tremendously in our defence of life, and establishing clear rules under which they can provide further aid in conjunction with the EU will help even more.”
Britain said on Wednesday night it would send 1,000 long-range attack drones to Ukraine as part of a further £260m military aid package, a day before prime minister Andy Burnham was due to travel to Berlin to co-chair a meeting of Kyiv’s European allies.
The commitment to support Ukraine’s deep strike campaign into Russia emerged a day after the US argued that Kyiv’s attacks on refineries and warehouses were ineffective and counter-productive, earning criticism from the UK and Germany.
“The UK will do everything we can to ensure Ukraine is able to defend itself,” Burnham said.

noticias.titulo: Israeli tanks cross ‘yellow line’ boundary into Hamas-controlled central Gaza
noticias.resumen: First incursion across boundary since ceasefire deal comes as Eisenkot seeks to form government without Netanyahu The Israeli military crossed into Hamas-controlled central Gaza on Wednesday in its first ground operation across the “yellow line” boundary since a fragile ceasefire was agreed last October, forcing dozens of displaced Palestinians to flee their tents. Israeli tanks rolled along the Salah al-Din road , Gaza’s main north-south route, a day after the US-backed Board of Peace, a body overseeing the ceasefire, accused Israel and Hamas of failing to honour their commitments to end host
noticias.texto:
The Israeli military crossed into Hamas-controlled central Gaza on Wednesday in its first ground operation across the “yellow line” boundary since a fragile ceasefire was agreed last October, forcing dozens of displaced Palestinians to flee their tents.
Israeli tanks rolled along the Salah al-Din road, Gaza’s main north-south route, a day after the US-backed Board of Peace, a body overseeing the ceasefire, accused Israel and Hamas of failing to honour their commitments to end hostilities.
An Israeli military spokesperson said troops were carrying out an operation targeting “Hamas infrastructure” west of the yellow line in central Gaza.
The military has not commented extensively on the operation, which came as the Israeli opposition politician, Gadi Eisenkot, has been seeking to form a government without the caretaker prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, who has built his political reputation on promises to keep Israel safe.
A Gaza security source told AFP there was “intense Israeli artillery shelling” north of Nuseirat refugee camp and reported Israeli military vehicles in central Gaza “amid ongoing gunfire and airstrikes since midday”.
Hamas condemned the Israeli raid and the forced displacement of Palestinians as “a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement” and a dangerous escalation. The Israeli military did not immediately respond to Hamas’s statement.
Residents reported hearing tank fire in the area. Palestinian medics said one person was killed in an Israeli airstrike near the site of the raid.
In separate incidents on Wednesday, Palestinian medics said two people were killed by Israeli fire, one in Deir al-Balah and the other in Gaza City. The Israeli military said it was unaware of any incident in Deir al-Balah and had struck a militant in Gaza City.
Israel has stepped up its attacks on Hamas, which it says has been regrouping and rearming. Hamas has accused Israel of trying to derail the US-brokered ceasefire agreed in October 2025.
Israeli strikes have continued since the ceasefire, and Hamas remains armed.
Last week, an Israeli airstrike on Nasser hospital in southern Gaza killed six people, including a surgeon and a disabled man, and wounded 28 others, according to the hospital director.
The body overseeing Donald Trump’s plan to end the war in Gaza has accused Israel and Hamas of failing to honour their commitments to end hostilities, leaving Palestinians in dire conditions and the ceasefire at risk of collapse.
In its second report to the UN security council since the truce began 13 months ago, the Trump-led Board of Peace said the gap between what was agreed and what was happening on the ground remained the biggest threat to the deal. The report, seen by Reuters, warned that “a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be sustained indefinitely”.
Gaza’s health authorities say at least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire came into effect. The Israeli military says five of its soldiers have been killed over the same period.
Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Gaza since Israel launched its military campaign in response to the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, in which about 1,200 people were killed.
Reuters and AFP contributed to this report

noticias.titulo: India has been named a ‘destination of the year’ for 2027 – here are insiders’ tips on travelling beyond the tropes
noticias.resumen: As tourism booms, three experienced female travellers give their take on how to make the most of travelling here • Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here The 13th-century Persian scholar Zakariyya al-Qazwini never travelled to India. But he catalogued it in his famous work The Wonders of Creation and Rarities of Existence, which drew on accounts of a distant land filled with “rarities par excellence”.
